packageRules.description: RustiCal moves as ONE: the five rustical_* crates (one workspace tag; build.rs refuses mixed tags) and the RustiCal image whose binary the Dockerfile copies (build.rs and the image test require the same release). Both come from the xarif fork (github.com/xarif-de/rustical, image registry.gitlab.com/xarif/docker/rustical) with tags v<upstream>-xarif.<n>: npm-semver would read the suffix as a prerelease and never propose it, hence the regex versioning (build = the fork release). Our own tags need no waiting period (minimumReleaseAge null; the fork already waits 24 h after upstream), and the group waits until all six parts see the new tag (minimumGroupSize: the image appears minutes after the git tag). Matched by dependency name: for a git dependency the package name is the repository URL.

One Rust version for the image build AND local dev/tests: the builder image (build/Dockerfile and the API-doc job in .gitlab-ci.yml, `rust:<x.y>-alpine`) and build/rust-toolchain.toml move in ONE PR. Until 2026-10-02 they were separate: the image (docker tags, no timestamps) updated at once, the toolchain file (Renovate's rust-toolchain manager, rust-version datasource WITH timestamps) waited the preset's 3-day minimumReleaseAge — so every Rust release left CI and `mise run test` on different compilers for days. build/Cargo.toml's rust-version is the MSRV floor and is not bumped.

build/rust-toolchain.toml is read by the custom regex manager below (docker datasource, same versions and timing as the builder image) instead of Renovate's rust-toolchain manager, whose timestamped datasource makes it lag the image.
rust-toolchain.toml takes a bare channel (`1.99`); a digest there would break rustup.

customManagers.description: Track the toolchain channel in build/rust-toolchain.toml against the official rust image tags (same versions as the builder image).
